html:
The First Anglo-Burmese War was fought from 1824 to 1826 between Burma and the British East India Company, after Burma's expansion into Assam and Manipur brought it to the border of British Bengal.

A British fleet took Rangoon, and after hard fighting and heavy losses to disease, a British army advanced up the Irrawaddy. By the Treaty of Yandabo, Burma gave up Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim and paid a large indemnity.

It was one of the costliest wars of British India. A second war in 1852 took Lower Burma, and the third war of 1885 ended the kingdom. See Alaungpaya's Konbaung dynasty and Arakan.
sum: The First Anglo-Burmese War was fought from 1824 to 1826 between Burma and the British East India Company, after Burma's expansion into Assam and Manipur brought it to the border of British Bengal.
